metadata.schedule_summary: Pembrolizumab 200 mg is given as a drip over about 30 minutes on Day 1 every 3 weeks (21 days). The hospital visit is longer because of checks and preparation. After complete surgery and platinum chemotherapy, the adjuvant course lasts up to 12 months. For metastatic cancer, treatment continues while it remains helpful and tolerable; the team may consider stopping after 24 months of sustained response without progression, or continuing when appropriate.

retrospective_audit_v08426.change: Explicit clinical attribution before immune hepatitis/nephritis actions; abnormal unclassified laboratory results require review, never automatic permanent stop.

supplemental_source.section: 4.4 immune-mediated hepatitis and nephritis: exclude other causes

clinical_governance.prescriptive_authority: Treatment initiated by a Consultant Medical Oncologist or a Consultant Medical Haematologist experienced in haematological malignancies, as applicable to the indication.
clinical_governance.dose_modification_note: Do not reduce pembrolizumab dose. Hold, discontinue or consider restart according to the specific toxicity and consultant review.
clinical_governance.disclaimer: Development encoding of NCCP 00455 v16; independent clinical and oncology pharmacy validation pending. Clinical use is not authorised.

indications.description: First-line metastatic NSCLC with PD-L1 TPS ≥50% and no EGFR mutation or ALK translocation.
Ipilimumab-refractory unresectable or advanced metastatic melanoma.
Locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma after prior platinum-containing chemotherapy.
Cisplatin-ineligible locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma with PD-L1 CPS ≥10.
Adjuvant treatment of completely resected stage III melanoma with lymph-node involvement.
First-line metastatic or unresectable recurrent HNSCC with PD-L1 CPS ≥1.
Relapsed/refractory classical Hodgkin lymphoma after ASCT failure or at least two prior therapies when ASCT is not an option.
Maintenance after induction chemotherapy for persistent, recurrent or metastatic cervical cancer with PD-L1 CPS ≥1.
First-line metastatic MSI-H or dMMR colorectal cancer.
Adjuvant treatment of completely resected stage IIB or IIC melanoma.
Adjuvant treatment of RCC at increased recurrence risk after nephrectomy, with or without resection of metastatic lesions.
Adjuvant NSCLC at high recurrence risk following complete resection and platinum-based chemotherapy; source stage IB–IIIA AJCC 7th edition, ECOG 0–1.

pembro_immune_hepatitis_assessed.label: Liver abnormality clinically assessed as immune-mediated hepatitis?
pembro_immune_hepatitis_assessed.help: Yes means the treating clinician has assessed immune-mediated toxicity and evaluated alternative causes; a raised laboratory result alone does not establish this. No or blank keeps an abnormal result in a clinical-review pathway. This does not require biopsy confirmation. EMA Keytruda IV SmPC §4.4; NCCP Table 1 applies to immune-related adverse reactions.

rules.explanation: Withhold uncontrolled adrenal insufficiency/hypophysitis, severe hyperthyroidism or immune diabetes with severe hyperglycaemia/DKA. Stabilise with specialist care; grade 2 adrenal/hypophysitis is held until controlled by hormone replacement.

action.recommendation: Withhold for type 1 diabetes with glucose >13.9 mmol/L; urgently assess for ketoacidosis. This threshold is not a generic rule for all hyperglycaemia.

action.recommendation: Withhold and arrange urgent hospital assessment for type 1 diabetes with ketoacidosis.

action.recommendation: Hypothyroidism may be managed with hormone replacement without interrupting pembrolizumab. This only addresses the thyroid domain and does not clear the whole regimen.

action.recommendation: After grade 3–4 endocrinopathy has improved to ≤grade 2 and is controlled with hormone replacement, continuation may be considered after steroid taper when needed. Consultant approval is required; do not apply an automatic generic grade 4 stop.

action.recommendation: Discontinue if the source conditions for continuation after severe endocrinopathy are not met; specialist review must establish the ongoing plan.

action.recommendation: Permanently discontinue if treatment-related toxicity has not recovered to grade 0–1 by 12 weeks after the last dose or toxicity steroids cannot taper to ≤10 mg/day prednisolone equivalent within 12 weeks. Reconcile specific endocrine exceptions before selecting this condition.

action.recommendation: NCCP Table 2 recommends no renal dose adjustment; none is expected for haemodialysis. This does not override active immune-nephritis or other toxicity holds.

action.recommendation: No adjustment is needed for mild hepatic impairment; no adjustment is expected for moderate/severe impairment. This does not override active immune-hepatitis rules; review clinical context.

action.recommendation: Adjuvant melanoma, RCC and NSCLC have a maximum 12-month course. Confirm completion and do not automatically continue beyond the source duration.

action.recommendation: At 24 months, consider discontinuation if there is sustained response and no progression; ongoing treatment may be appropriate. This is an individual decision, not a mandatory fixed cap.

action.recommendation: Abnormal liver result crosses an immune-toxicity table threshold, but immune causality has not been established. Obtain prompt clinical assessment, investigate alternative causes and document the treatment decision. Do not administer automatically or apply permanent immune-toxicity discontinuation from an isolated laboratory result. No dose reduction is calculated.

eligibility: Use the exact indication-specific criteria and NCCP PD-1/PD-L1 retreatment guidance.
Metastatic NSCLC: first-line stage IV disease, validated TPS ≥50%, no EGFR mutation/ALK translocation, ECOG 0–1.
Adjuvant NSCLC: high recurrence risk, complete resection and prior platinum chemotherapy, source stage IB–IIIA AJCC7, ECOG 0–1; no metastatic TPS50 gate.
exclusions: Apply indication-specific criteria, including HNSCC exclusion for progression within six months of curative-intent systemic therapy.
monitoring: Baseline blood count, renal/liver profile, glucose and thyroid function; validated biomarker testing when indicated.
Blood count, renal/liver profile and glucose before each cycle; thyroid function every 3–6 weeks, including during the 42-day schedule.
Cortisol when clinically indicated; disease assessment/imaging according to the consultant treatment plan.
Assess immune toxicity during and after treatment.
dose_modifications: No dose reduction. Apply toxicity-specific withhold, permanent-stop, restart and 12-week criteria.
No renal adjustment; no adjustment expected during dialysis. Mild hepatic: no adjustment; moderate/severe: none expected. Active immune organ injury follows Table 1.

supportive_care.mapping_basis: Pembrolizumab monotherapy 200 mg every 3 weeks, source minimal emetic risk.
